cards.headline:
Flow matching takes on
four-stem music separation
cards.body: FLOMSS tests flow matching as a generative way to split full-band music into vocals, bass, drums and other stems.

blocks.x: FLOMSS: Generative Music Source Separation by Flow Matching, by Shuyang Cui, Yuki Mitsufuji and 11 co-authors, was submitted to arXiv on 13 Oct 2026.

Music source separation (MSS) has been conventionally addressed by discriminative methods. Flow matching has recently emerged as a strong generative paradigm, and the authors systematically investigate it for MSS in a four-source (Vocals, Bass, Drums, Other) setting in full-band stereo.

They study prediction targets, flow paths, single-source versus multi-source modeling, and mixture consistency constraints. Beyond signal-to-distortion ratio, they evaluate MSS methods with spectral and embedding-based metrics as well as a listening test, providing a comprehensive benchmark.

blocks.cap: Figure 1: Stepwise behavior of OT-CFM-x for Vocals across Midpoint ODE solver steps. Dashed gray lines indicate the discriminative baseline.

blocks.x: On MUSDB18-HQ, FLOMSS surpasses prior generative methods and a same-backbone discriminative baseline on spectral and embedding-based metrics. It also improves Mel and FD over strong discriminative methods, although SDR remains lower.

The authors identify a distributional–reconstruction trade-off in generative MSS and present FLOMSS as an open-source framework, with code to be released upon acceptance. A demo is available at ik4sumii.github.io/FLOMSS.
